transcript: A lot of meetings are really presentations with a calendar invite. Here's when a video saves everyone time, and when to keep the meeting.
If the content is mostly one-way, a video often wins. It reaches the manager, finance and IT, and lands in their morning, whether that's Perth or London.
But keep the meeting for real conversation. A good rule: if it's mostly you talking, send a video. If it's mostly them talking, meet.
A video only saves time if people watch it. Keep it short, tell them why it matters up front, and end with one clear next step.
Instead of waiting a week for a follow-up meeting, send a five-minute narrated deck the next morning. The next meeting becomes questions, not a presentation.
Put what you'd say in the speaker notes. On Pro, a.i. directs the video, so your proposal lands like a produced pitch. Try it at powerpoint2vid.com.
